html:
A hand-woven cotton cloth of Burkina Faso, whose name means woven cloth of the homeland, which Thomas Sankara made the official dress of civil servants in the 1980s.

Sankara wanted Burkinabe to wear their own cotton, spun and woven by local women, instead of imported cloth, as part of his campaign for self-reliance. The rule lapsed after his death, but the cloth came back into fashion in the 2010s, and presidents since the 2014 uprising have promoted it again. Burkina Faso is one of Africa's largest cotton growers, though most is exported raw.
sum: A hand-woven cotton cloth of Burkina Faso, whose name means woven cloth of the homeland, which Thomas Sankara made the official dress of civil servants in the 1980s.
